verdict.summary: Graph assembly mostly correct. All cross-batch references resolved, no dangling edges. However, suffers from ID-format inconsistency across batches, 62 nodes with __nofilepath__ placeholder IDs, 98 nodes with unknown/non-schema types, and zero complexity differentiation (all 'moderate'). Edge relations are split between lowercase (49) and uppercase (10+5) naming conventions.

issues.detail: 10 node types not in canonical schema: method(26), constant(18), config-value(14), python_module(13), subpackage(10), config_file(5), package(2), shell_pattern(2), pattern(2), test_file(2), function-group(2), documentation(1).
issues.recommendation: Either extend the schema to include these types or map them to canonical equivalents (method→function, constant→concept, config-value→config, python_module→module, subpackage→module, etc.).

issues.detail: All 300 nodes have complexity='moderate'. No simple, complex, or critical annotations exist.
issues.recommendation: If the extraction subagent didn't provide complexity, consider heuristics: files <50 lines → simple, >200 lines → complex, core ROS nodes/control-loop → critical.

issues.detail: Batch 3 uses nonstandard ID format (e.g., 'file-train/scripts/export_policy.sh' instead of 'file:train/scripts/export_policy.sh'). These were fixed by the merge script (71 bare path→file: corrections).
issues.recommendation: Fix the batch-3 extraction to emit canonical 'type:path' IDs consistently.

issues.detail: Batch 5 uses simple names without prefix (e.g., 'DeployConfig', 'ControlLoop'). These were prefixed to 'class:__nofilepath__:DeployConfig' during merge.
issues.recommendation: Batch 5 extraction should include proper type-prefixed IDs and file paths.

issues.detail: Batch 6 uses descriptive IDs (e.g., 'Pi05LoraTrainer.run', 'main@train.cli.train') without canonical type prefix or file path in the ID.
issues.recommendation: Standardize to 'method:Pi05LoraTrainer.run' and 'function:main@train.cli.train' with proper file fields.

issues.detail: Some nodes use properties.description (batches 1-4 style), others use flat summary/docString (batches 3,5,6 style). Merge script did not normalize these.
issues.recommendation: Normalize all nodes to use a single description field convention (e.g., always under properties.description).

issues.detail: 62 nodes have '__nofilepath__' placeholder in their ID, meaning the extraction lacked a file path. These use source_file/source_location instead. This is acceptable for structural nodes but makes ID-based lookups fragile.
issues.recommendation: When source_file is available, reconstruct the canonical ID (e.g., 'class:deploy/src/pi05/deploy/config/schema.py:DeployConfig'). Only use __nofilepath__ when truly no file context exists.

issues.detail: Some file nodes (batch 5/6 style) lack language/fileCategory properties that batch-4 nodes consistently include.
issues.recommendation: Ensure all file-type nodes include language and fileCategory in their properties.

cross_batch_reference_verification.detail: All 34 symbols from the cross-batch import map were found in the assembled graph (100% resolution rate).

issues.detail: Edge relation names mix lowercase (calls, uses, imports, composes, etc. = 49 unique) and UPPERCASE (CALLS, USES, COMPOSES, OWNS, PRODUCES, etc. = 10 unique). UPPERCASE relations appear only in batch-5/6 edges.
issues.recommendation: Normalize all relations to lowercase for consistency. The mixed case suggests two different extraction agents produced the edges.

issues.detail: Some relations are very generic ('related', 'references', 'uses') and could be more specific where the source code indicates a concrete relationship.
examples: 'normalization and action_codec are sibling data modules' → could be 'sibling_package'
'config:deploy.yaml:runtime overrides common runtime settings' → 'overrides' is fine

issues.detail: ~20 edges involve concept nodes (abstract concepts without file backing) connecting to concrete nodes. These are high-level architectural connections, useful for overview but less precise than code-level edges.
64 input edges were dropped during merge because source or target node IDs couldn't be resolved. This is 17% of the input edge set.
issues.recommendation: Investigate which batches contributed the dropped edges. If batch-3 nonstandard IDs or batch-5 unnamed nodes were involved, fixing those upstream would reduce edge loss.
